summary: Anthropic opened a research preview of the Model Hardware Standard (MHS), a shared specification and driver protocol that lets AI agents (including Claude) discover, control and orchestrate lab and manufacturing hardware such as liquid handlers, robotic arms and microscopes, piloted with partners including Genentech and University of Washington labs.

mechanisms.reason: The standard is explicitly built to let agents run autonomous, round-the-clock physical workflows across multiple devices, extending agentic execution beyond software into lab/manufacturing hardware.
mechanisms.quote: MHS also helps researchers and engineers more readily orchestrate autonomous, round-the-clock experiments and workflows, with agents able to reason through each step in an experiment, update parameters in real time, and, in some cases, recover from hardware errors without intervention.

practices.reason: MHS defines a concrete driver/primitive architecture (read/write commands, MCP/CLI/API control, chaining into code files) that an engineering team building agent-hardware pipelines could implement, though it is new and hardware-specific.
practices.quote: When the agent needs to execute long-running tasks or operate devices faster than its online reasoning would allow, it can chain together driver commands from one or more devices in code files.

notable_reason: This is a genuinely new class of agent deployment -- AI agents directly operating physical lab and manufacturing hardware via a shared standard -- with named research and industry partners, which is distinct from routine model or product updates.
